title: Meet the nested if: a choice inside a choice
idea: A nested if puts a second decision INSIDE the body of a first if. The inner question is only asked when the outer one was already True. Meet it with visible output.

exercises.prompt: Sometimes you only ask a second question AFTER the first answer is yes. Example: 'Is the shop open? If so, do they have milk?' What is a 'nested if'?
options: An if written inside the body of another if
exercises.explanation: Nested means 'one inside another'. The inner if lives inside the outer if's indented body, so it is only reached when the outer condition was True.
The outer if is True (logged_in), so we step inside. There the inner if is True too (is_admin), so 'Admin panel' prints.
Outer if is still True, so we go inside. Now the inner if is False, so its else runs: 'User page'.
The outer if is False, so Python skips its whole body - the inner if is never even looked at - and runs the outer else: 'Please log in'.

exercises.prompt: The inner if is only checked when the outer if's condition was True.
exercises.explanation: Yes. The inner if lives inside the outer body. If the outer condition is False, the whole body (including the inner if) is skipped.

exercises.prompt: Why does the inner if need to be indented MORE than the outer if?
options: The extra indent shows it belongs inside the outer if's body
It makes the code run faster
exercises.explanation: Indentation is how Python groups lines. Deeper indent = 'this belongs to the block above it'. The inner if sits inside the outer body.

exercises.prompt: A nested if asks the second question only in some cases, not every time.
exercises.explanation: That is the whole point. The second decision is reached only on the path where the first condition held - a choice inside a choice.
has_ticket is True, so we go inside. seat_free is False, so the inner else runs: 'Stand'.

exercises.prompt: For the ticket code above, match each situation to what prints.
exercises.explanation: The seat question only matters once you have a ticket. No ticket means the inner question is never asked.

exercises.prompt: The big idea of a nested if is...
options: ask a second question only after the first one was answered yes
ask both questions at the same time
exercises.explanation: A nested if is a choice inside a choice: the inner decision is reached only along the branch where the outer condition was True.
